entities.name: Li Gonglin
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Li Gonglin, style name Boshi (伯時), art name Longmian Jushi, was a Chinese antiquarian, painter, and politician during the Northern Song dynasty (960-1127).

He was born into a family of modest means and received a classical education, which he later used to critique the excesses of the imperial court.

As a prominent figure in the Northern Song, Li Gonglin played a key role in shaping the dynasty's cultural and artistic identity. He was a prolific writer, producing numerous essays and poems that explored the intersection of Confucianism and Buddhism.

Despite his influential work, Li Gonglin's legacy was largely forgotten during the Yuan dynasty (1271-1368), but his ideas experienced a resurgence during the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).

The scholar-historian and philosopher, Zhou Youguang, once wrote, 'Li Gonglin's essays are a window into the soul of the Northern Song.'
